paper.title_en: Anisotropic wormhole solutions and Stability Analysis in Finsler-Randers Geometry
paper.abstract_en: In the present paper, we constructed the structural properties and stability behavior of wormhole solutions within the framework of Finsler-Randers geometry, with special attention to the role of different energy distributions. As a generalized extension of Riemannian geometry, the Finsler geometry naturally accommodates anisotropic effects and thus provides a broader mathematical setting for the study of gravitational and cosmological systems. Employing the osculating Riemannian formalism, we developed wormhole models associated with non commutative geometry inspired matter sources and different linear, logarithmic and power-law shape functions. The impact of the Finslerian parameter is examined systematically, and the relevant energy conditions are tested for each case. The solutions obtained in this framework offer insight into the physical plausibility of traversable wormholes and may help clarify some of the long-standing difficulties related to their matter content. The stability of wormhole is also determined by the Herrera cracking condition and Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff (TOV) equation. Our results suggest that a combination of Finsler geometry with the osculating-Randers approach provides a promising framework for constructing stable and physically acceptable wormhole spacetimes. The study is supported by exact analytical solutions together with two-dimensional and three-dimensional graphical analysis, thereby contributing to a deeper understanding of anisotropic spacetime geometry, generalized gravitational phenomena, and stability of the wormhole.
